extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, facility environmental compliance staff, State and Federal permitting authorities, and consultants advising on CCR closure/corrective action
extracted.subtask_short: legacy CCR closure and corrective action
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and performance standards for corrective action, closure, and post-closure care of legacy CCR (coal combustion residuals) surface impoundments, including timelines, remedy selection, and equivalency/deferral procedures tied to permitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective measures assessment (ACM) scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The corrective action program includes initiating an ACM to prevent further releases, to remediate any releases, and to restore affected areas to original conditions, as specified in §257.96(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACM must address prevention, remediation, and restoration; it is the vehicle to assess and compare corrective measures and identify remedies that meet prescribed standards. EPA expects owners/operators to use site characterization and groundwater modeling where available to evaluate alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACM initiation and completion timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACM must be initiated within 90 days of determining an SSL (statistically significant level) has occurred, and then completed within another 90 days; an extension not to exceed 60 days may be warranted due to site-specific conditions or circumstances (i.e., completion within 180–240 days after determining an SSL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timeline was not modified in the final rule; commenters suggesting changes to these deadlines were outside the scope. EPA believes existing site characterization (e.g., geology, groundwater flow, waste streams) can support completing an ACM within these deadlines in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy selection standards including groundwater protection
rubrics_metrics.description: After completion of the ACM the owner/operator must select a remedy that meets prescribed standards, including a requirement that the remedy attain the groundwater protection standards (see §257.97(a) and (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the ACM is complete, a public meeting must be held and community input considered; remedy selection should occur as soon as feasible. Implementation of source-control measures (e.g., closure by removal) does not negate the requirement to implement the groundwater remediation portion of the remedy within a reasonable time, in accordance with the schedule in the remedy selection report (see §257.97(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial activities initiation deadline after remedy selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The corrective action program requires the owner/operator to initiate remedial activities within 90 days of selecting a remedy (see §257.98(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation of remedial activities must follow remedy selection promptly to address releases; EPA emphasizes timely implementation in both active-life and post-closure contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of impacts to nearby surface water and groundwater receptors
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing corrective measures and selecting a remedy, the owner/operator should consider the impact of the corrective measures on the water quality and safety of the nearest surface water bodies and the nearest private and/or public groundwater wells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects remedy assessments to account for off-site receptors and nearby drinking-water sources when evaluating alternatives and specifying timelines/controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply closure and post-closure requirements to legacy CCR surface impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments are required to comply with the existing closure and post-closure care requirements in §§257.100 through 257.104 (including §257.101(a) requiring closure of impoundments constructed without a composite liner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded that legacy impoundments pose risks similar to active/inactive impoundments and therefore must follow the same closure/post-closure criteria; the D.C. Circuit decision (USWAG) supports requiring closure of unlined/clay-lined impoundments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to initiate closure (extended)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA extended the deadline to initiate closure for legacy CCR surface impoundments to 48 months from promulgation (the proposal had originally required initiation within 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considers 48 months adequate to address accessibility, seasonality, overlapping regulatory requirements, and resource constraints cited by commenters. Facilities with accessibility or critical-infrastructure sequencing issues should plan staging/scheduling in that period; EPA will coordinate if actual reliability concerns are demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure performance standards (§257.102) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Closures of legacy CCR surface impoundments must meet the performance standards in §257.102(c) (clean closure) or §257.102(d) (closure with waste in place). All closures initiated after the effective date, and closures not completed prior to the effective date, must comply with these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility can certify a prior closure meets §257.102(c) or demonstrate compliance with §257.102(d), it need only post documentation; otherwise, closure must be brought into compliance. EPA will defer application of §257.102 for certain previously closed units pending permitting equivalency determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of closure method and mandatory performance compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner/operator may choose either clean closure (removal) or closure with waste in place, but must meet all the performance standards for the chosen option; if unable to meet the standards for one option (or part of a unit), the facility must use the alternative option and meet its standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation does not prefer one option; selection must be justified by ability to meet the full set of performance criteria for that option (see 40 CFR 257.102(a)–(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for closure with waste in place if performance standards are met
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will not categorically prohibit legacy impoundments from closing with waste in place under §257.102(d); both clean closure and closure with waste in place can be equally protective provided all requisite performance standards in §257.102 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters claiming closure-in-place is inherently inadequate must demonstrate why performance standards cannot be met; absent that, closure-in-place is an acceptable option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral/equivalency for prior closures pending permitting
rubrics_metrics.description: For units that were closed prior to the rule under different standards that are likely equivalent to §257.102, EPA is deferring the requirement to demonstrate compliance with §257.102 until a permit authority evaluates the adequacy of the closure during permitting. Criteria are used to ensure the prior standards were substantially equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deferral is limited to the §257.102 performance standard requirement only; all other applicable requirements (e.g., groundwater monitoring, corrective action) continue to apply, and EPA retains authority to act on urgent threats (e.g., under 42 U.S.C. 6973). Equivalency determinations and procedures are modeled on similar processes for hazardous waste interim status units under §270.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for previously compliant closures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a facility can certify that its prior closure meets the performance standards in §257.102(c), it only needs to post documentation that it meets the standard rather than re-close the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA never intended to require re-closure where the performance standards have already been met. Where prior closure was performed under other Federal or State programs but is demonstrably equivalent, permitting will evaluate whether additional measures are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of groundwater monitoring and corrective action obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where the requirement to meet §257.102 is deferred for a previously closed unit, groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements remain applicable to those units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral does not eliminate monitoring or corrective action obligations; those safeguards remain in force to mitigate potential risks until a permitting authority makes an equivalency determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: National criteria and prohibition on site-specific-only approach
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must set minimum national criteria for CCR units (per RCRA sections 1008(a)(3) and 4004(a)); EPA cannot rely exclusively on site-specific risk assessments or corrective action alone to avoid a national closure requirement for legacy impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The D.C. Circuit (USWAG) rejected arguments that a national closure requirement is unnecessary because not all impoundments are leaking or because corrective action could substitute. EPA must demonstrate through the rulemaking record that national criteria will achieve the statutory standard across sites; permitting can subsequently adjudicate site-specific legal/factual issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of inaccessible or redeveloped legacy impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments claiming closure is infeasible where legacy impoundments lie beneath infrastructure or redevelopment must provide concrete examples and data; absent demonstrated infeasibility, EPA expects closure can be staged/scheduled within the regulatory timeframe (now 48 months) and will coordinate to avoid critical infrastructure disruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considered overfill examples and evidence that redeveloped sites can still contribute to groundwater contamination; facilities should plan for staged outages or engineering measures (e.g., slurry walls) to address accessibility constraints rather than expect blanket exemptions.
